title: Trump pardons Rod Blagojevich in an Illinois federal corruption case
description_short: Trump granted Rod Blagojevich a full pardon on February 10, 2025, in a Northern District of Illinois corruption case.
description_medium: On February 10, 2025, President Donald Trump granted Rod Blagojevich a full and unconditional pardon in United States v. Blagojevich, a Northern District of Illinois case. DOJ lists his sentence and offenses including wire fraud under color of official right, attempted extortion, and solicitation of a bribe. The official record names one recipient; it does not support the original claim about several New Jersey politicians or a political exchange.
description_long:
On February 10, 2025, President Donald Trump granted a full and unconditional pardon to Rod Blagojevich. The executive warrant names the case as United States v. Blagojevich in the Northern District of Illinois, and names Blagojevich as the recipient. The DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney lists a December 7, 2011 sentence of 168 months’ imprisonment as amended, 24 months’ supervised release, and a $20,000 fine. It identifies offenses including wire fraud under color of official right, attempted extortion under color of official right, conspiracy to solicit and solicitation of a bribe, and making false statements.

These primary records support one February 10 pardon in a federal corruption case. They do not support the earlier description of several New Jersey politicians: the warrant identifies one recipient and an Illinois federal case. They also provide no evidence that the pardon was a political transaction, rewarded loyalty, or reflected a finding that the conviction was unjust. The proposal therefore retains the dated pardon event while removing the unsupported number, New Jersey identity, and motive claims.

proposal.description_long: On January 22, 2025, Montclair Patch reported criticism in New Jersey of President Donald Trump’s January 20 clemency for people charged in connection with the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack. U.S. Representative Mikie Sherrill said the pardons undermined the rule of law and objected to clemency for people convicted of violence against police. State Senator John McKeon, whose district includes Essex County communities, called the pardons a “disgraceful affront” to the justice system and said they undermined accountability for the attack on the peaceful transfer of power. Patch also reported supportive views from some Republican officials, so the local political response was mixed. The Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney states that Trump granted clemency on January 20 for offenses relating to the January 6 events. Together, these sources support an account of New Jersey officials’ public reaction to the clemency. They do not support the original claim that Trump pardoned corrupt New Jersey politicians, that the recipients were politicians, or that the grants were a political exchange. Those allegations are omitted.

proposal.description_long: On January 22, 2025, Montclair Patch reported criticism in New Jersey of President Donald Trump’s January 20 clemency for people charged in connection with the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack. U.S. Representative Mikie Sherrill said the pardons undermined the rule of law and objected to clemency for people convicted of violence against police. State Senator John McKeon, whose district includes Essex County communities, called the pardons a “disgraceful affront” to the justice system and said they undermined accountability for the attack on the peaceful transfer of power. Patch also reported supportive views from some Republican officials, so the local political response was mixed. The Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney states that Trump granted clemency on January 20 for offenses relating to the January 6 events. Together, these sources support an account of New Jersey officials’ public reaction to the clemency. They do not support the original claim that Trump pardoned corrupt New Jersey politicians, that the recipients were politicians, or that the grants were a political exchange. Those allegations are omitted.

The DOJ confirms the clemency concerned January 6 offenses; Patch also reported differing local reactions. The reporting does not say the critics were recipients or establish a political exchange.
